### ↩︎ Cleared (dismissed — do not re-raise)

No over-engineering candidate targeted a ratified reserved seam: the E02-3 attackers pre-filed the sanctioned seams (`LipschitzConfig.mode`, the hydro storage/filling penalties, `historical_years`) under Positives with their mirror citations, so none re-entered the candidate set. The four dismissals below are merit-based (not sanctioned seams); each is cleared so the re-raise checker treats it as retired:

- **B-perf-00** — At baseline `tokenize` (generic.rs:629) is reached only via `parse_relation` <- `convert`'s per-constraint load-time loop (line 489) — the constraint-file-to-struct conversion, never the SDDP training/simulation hot paths enumerated in architecture-rules.md. The `Vec<char>` collect (line 631) is deliberate: it gives O(1) indexed two-char lookahead (`chars.get(i+1)` for `==`/`<=`/`>=`) and lets every error report a char-offset position (`at position {i}`) a human counting characters can locate;
- **B-perf-01** — The evidence resolves at baseline: `inline` (named_expression_inline.rs:57) builds its `HashMap<&str,&ParsedExpression>` index per top-level call, and `resolve_split_side` (generic.rs:1254-1255) does a linear `table.iter().any(...)` membership scan then calls `inline(&vec![...],table)`, rebuilding the index and allocating a one-element Vec for a single reference. Both call sites run inside `convert`'s per-constraint load-time loop (line 489), not a hot path.
- **B-perf-03** — Mechanism confirmed at baseline: `parse_inflow_history` (inflow_history.rs:144-152) maps every parsed `InflowHistoryRow` into a parallel `Vec<WindowedRecord>` consumed only by `validate_windowed_records` on the next line, then dropped. But this is a single O(rows) linear pass of a 4-field `Copy` struct (memcpy-able), dominated by O(rows) work already unconditionally present on the same rows: the parquet decode loop that builds `rows` from the record batches (rows.push at line 128) and the subsequent `rows.sort_by` (line 137, an O(rows log rows) pass).
- **C-over-engineering-00** — At the baseline all three enums derive serde::Serialize plus schemars::JsonSchema under #[serde(rename_all="snake_case")] (estimation.rs:15-18, scenario_source.rs:70-73, training.rs:106-109), so each exports a string-only JSON enum schema. serde's DERIVED Deserialize for a unit-variant enum accepts both the bare string ("pacf") and serde's externally-tagged single-key-map form ({"pacf":null});

#### Phase-1 uncertainty-store notes

Alignment hints only (Epic 9 adjudicates). The seam findings tagged `advances-1` mark where the Phase-1 `Switchable<T>` uncertainty store would form: `StochasticContext` (`context.rs`) is today both a computed store (five precomputed components) and a config/layout echo, and `ForwardSamplerConfig` (`sampling/mod.rs`) straddles the generation-side and realized-value halves. The fitted-process code (PAR estimation in `par/`, opening-tree generation in `tree/`, seed derivation) stays generation-only; the standardized realized libraries and the sampler are the store side. No fix is executed here.

Narrowed to a missed error class, not a corrupted report: because StudySetup::new and new_with_boundary_requirements take no artifact argument, they cannot satisfy the patch protocol StudyParams::scalar_parameters' own rustdoc mandates, so the two validate paths run build_resolved_parameters on an empty table whenever config.policy.boundary is configured, and validate's documented exit-0 contract is therefore broken for exactly the three ResolvedParametersError variants cobre_io::validation::scalar_parameters does not duplicate (MissingSeason, PerStageBlockCoverage, MissingSpecificProductivity), with is_block_varying returning false on a miss collapsing a PerStageBlock row set silently and with no assert. Conceded from the candidate: no boundary-reconciliation fact validate reports reads ResolvedParameters, so nothing validate prints is wrong; the setup is built and discarded; and the validate.rs:234 mirrors-the-run-path comment concerns boundary-requirement ordering, not the paramete…

- **Evidence:** The scalar-parameter table is a two-phase init with no type-level enforcement of phase 2. from_config writes Vec::new() and its own comment delegates the patch to 'each setup caller'; new_with_boundary_requirements patches params.boundary and NOTHING else before delegating to from_broadcast_params, and new delegates straight to it. So the only two constructors that take (system, config, stochastic, hydro_models) build the whole StudySetup -- including stage templates -- against an EMPTY table. The consequence is n… Re-derive: `git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-sddp/src/setup/params.rs | sed -n '174,177p;335,341p'; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-sddp/src/setup/mod.rs | sed -n '342,397p';…`

Either take the loaded Vec<ScalarParameter> as a parameter of new / new_with_boundary_requirements and drop the field's placeholder role in from_config, or split the type so a StudySetup can only be built from a params value whose scalar table has been supplied (an unpatched value is not accepted by from_broadcast_params). Independently of which, ResolvedParameters::get must stop returning 0.0 on a miss in release: a miss is a build-time defect, not a datum, so it belongs as a construction-time error at the LP-build site rather than a silent sentinel behind a debug_assert -- this is the fail-loud shape already on the open follow-up list. Fixing get alone is not sufficient and fixing the constructors alone is not sufficient: the first without the second turns a silent-wrong validate into an abort, the second without the first leaves the sentinel live for any future caller. **Performance** — 3 minted

**PD-035 · Sev C · duplication · effort S · confidence high**
Only the symmetric-matrix half of the title survives as a bit-exact free win: `l2_distance_matrix` (noise_key.rs:223-243) evaluates every off-diagonal pair's L2 twice and computes the zero diagonal, and mirroring plus a skipped diagonal leaves every entry bit-identical. The whole-tour `tour_cost` recomputation in `two_opt_improve` (174-191) is real but is demoted from removable redundancy to a semantics-changing perf-sweep item, because the full sum is what keeps the accept test at 182 and the cross-start winner at 212 functions of the tours and the matrix alone, and because a path reversal changes only ONE edge at `j == n_o - 1`. The per-start `nearest_neighbor_tour` buffer allocations (141-142) do not survive at all: they are once-per-study-setup work outside the hot-path allocation ban.

- **Station:** cobre-sddp (sddp, sub-station 5a, lens performance; ingest ref 5a-performance-00)
- **Baseline:** `077dbe2c287b92c2d0c6a12d5f67c2c0cb83c39c`
- **Anchors:** `crates/cobre-sddp/src/stochastic/noise_key.rs::two_opt_improve`, `crates/cobre-sddp/src/stochastic/noise_key.rs::tour_cost`, `crates/cobre-sddp/src/stochastic/noise_key.rs::shortest_chain_path`, `crates/cobre-sddp/src/stochastic/noise_key.rs::l2_distance_matrix`, `crates/cobre-sddp/src/stochastic/noise_key.rs::nearest_neighbor_tour`, `crates/cobre-sddp/src/stochastic/noise_key.rs::apply_chain_order`
- **Evidence:** `two_opt_improve` calls `tour_cost`, a pass over the whole tour, once per candidate segment reversal, and the reversal loop is the quadratic (i, j) sweep repeated under `while improved`. `shortest_chain_path` runs that whole improvement for each of n_o nearest-neighbour starts, and `apply_chain_order` calls it once per study stage carrying at least three openings. A path 2-opt reversal changes exactly two edges, so the accept/reject test needs two matrix reads rather than a whole-tour sum. `l2_distance_matrix` wri… Re-derive: `git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-sddp/src/stochastic/noise_key.rs | sed -n '132,146p;174,222p;223,266p'; git grep -n 'build_noise_key_table' 077dbe2c -- crates/c…`
- **Fix-shape:** Two halves with different risk, and they should be queued separately. The byte-exact half: fill the distance matrix symmetrically by writing the mirrored entry instead of recomputing it and skip the zero diagonal, since `(a - b) * (a - b)` equals `(b - a) * (b - a)` exactly in IEEE arithmetic and the per-pair summation order is unchanged, so the matrix is bit-identical; and hoist the nearest-neighbour tour and visited buffers out of the per-start loop, reusing them by clear-and-refill, which changes no value at all. Both leave the winning permutation identical, so the parity goldens in tests/parity.rs and tests/common/parity_hash.rs, the rank-invariance harness in tests/common/permute.rs, and `mpiexec` at one rank versus two ranks all reproduce unchanged and no golden moves. The half that does move goldens: replacing the whole-tour recomputation with the two-edge delta a path reversal actually implies changes the floating-point basis of the accept/reject comparison, can flip a marginal reversal, and so can change the winning permutation. Per .claude/rules/sddp.md section Bac…

- **Fix-shape:** Accumulate per-hydro sums and counts in one pass over inflow_history() before the parallel map, into a container indexed by the hydro's canonical declaration position, and pass the resolved mean into fit_one_hydro the way the other pre-grouped maps are already passed. #### Architecture (CD)

**CD-099 · Sev B · leaky-boundary · effort S · confidence high**
The infrastructure-crate set is hand-written at sites the gate never pairs: its own header at check-infra-genericity.sh:5-8, SCAN_DIRS at :62-68, and the hard-rule bullet at CLAUDE.md:39-41. No gate at the pin refuses a state where the crates scanned and the crates the rule names differ, even though comment_scan.sh:43-68 already performs that class of divergence check for the cfg(test) boundary as a blocking step at ci.yml:264-267. Conceded from the title: the curated literal list is correct and must not be derived from workspace membership, and the single-line amendment the layering brief L1 row prescribes does extend coverage to a future L1 crate. The residue is the absent divergence check between the gate's scanned set and the rule's named set, not the hand-kept list.

- **Station:** build-ci — build/CI/scripts/schemas/docs (lens architecture; ingest ref architecture-00)
- **Baseline:** `077dbe2c287b92c2d0c6a12d5f67c2c0cb83c39c`
- **Anchors:** `scripts/ci/check-infra-genericity.sh:62`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:261`, `CLAUDE.md:39`
- **Enforcement:** blocking — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `quality-scripts`, step "Infra genericity gate" (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:262`) — gate-census.json row for scripts/ci/check-infra-genericity.sh
- **Evidence:** Two independent literal enumerations of the same five crates: SCAN_DIRS at :62-68 (cobre-core, cobre-io, cobre-solver, cobre-stochastic, cobre-comm) and the prose bullet at CLAUDE.md:39-41 (the same five names in the same order). Membership is a hardcoded path list, not derived from the workspace or from a layer declaration, so a crate added to the workspace is outside the rule by default -- silence, not failure. Nothing compares the two lists: `git grep -n 'cobre-stochastic' 077dbe2c -- scripts/ci` returns only check-infra-genericity.sh, so no gate cross-checks the prose enumeration against SCAN_DIRS. The layering brief's L1 row states the rule extends to the future `cobre-model` / `cobre-network` ONLY by amending the CI grep's crate list; the target-state coverage therefore depends on a person remembering two files in two languages at once. `git show 077dbe2c:scripts/ci/check-infra-genericity.sh | sed -n '62,68p'; git show 077dbe2c:CLAUDE.md | sed -n '39,41p'; git show 077dbe2c:.github/workflows/ci.yml | sed -n '248p;261,262p'`
- **Fix-shape:** Amend in place, and make the pairing mechanical rather than remembered. The durable shape is to let one of the two sites own the crate list and have the other derive or verify it: either the gate reads the layer membership from a single declared list and the prose points at that list by name instead of re-enumerating it, or the gate grows a self-check that fails when the crates it scans and the crates the rule names diverge. Either way the edit that adds a future L1 crate touches one authoritative list and the gate refuses to pass while the other site disagrees. Do not build a new gate framework or a new shared scan library for this -- the existing blocking gate and its single `quality-scripts` step are the right home, and a new framework would be a one-consumer abstraction.
- **Two-site rule (infra-genericity):** rule = `CLAUDE.md:39` — Infrastructure crate genericity hard rule (:39-41); script = `scripts/ci/check-infra-genericity.sh:62` — SCAN_DIRS (:62-68); ci_step = `.github/workflows/ci.yml:261` — quality-scripts job (:248), step `Infra genericity gate` (:261-262) — all three site kinds named; a fix that touched fewer would be returned for sharpening.
- **Alignment:** advances-1 (provisional; Epic 9 adjudicates against the L0-L4 target-layering brief — Part IV §IV.1 — extending the genericity rule to the future L1 crates `cobre-model` / `cobre-network` 'means amending the rule text and the CI grep's crate list, not assuming it extends' (plans/generalizing/beyond-sddp-generalization.md:1303; layering brief §1 L1 row))
- **Alignment note:** the defender proposed advances-0b (the carve is when the list first changes); the house records advances-1 because the rule's coverage is a Phase-1 purification obligation the brief pins to this exact edit, and the carve does not by itself add a crate to SCAN_DIRS (attacker hint advances-1, defender hint advances-0b).
- **Calibration:** the infrastructure-crate set is hand-written at three sites the gate never pairs (its own header :5-8, SCAN_DIRS :62-68, the hard-rule bullet CLAUDE.md:39-41) and no gate refuses a divergent state — a bounded set of named edit sites, not a spreading structure: Sev B on the CD-010 leaky-boundary precedent.
- **Needs-human (owner gate):** Owner must choose where the single owner of the infra-crate set sits: CLAUDE.md:39-41 keeps its enumeration pinned by a new divergence check in the gate, or the bullet becomes a shape-only pointer to the gate's list, since doc-integrity section 3 mode 1 admits either and the choice decides which site an amendment edits first.
- **Queued to:** alignment

**CD-100 · Sev B · asymmetry · effort S · confidence high**
Narrower than the title: ci.yml alone carries the gap — its pull_request filter is [main] at :6-7 against a push filter of [main, develop] at :4-5, so no ci.yml job (the quality-scripts gates at :248-300 plus clippy :154, fmt :246, schemas :339, docs-examples :360) evaluates a develop-targeted change before it is merged. The claim does NOT extend to 'no CI workflow' — mpi-slurm.yml:5-6 names develop under pull_request and release.yml:42 / release-python.yml:26 have no base-branch filter, so all three run on a develop pull request — nor to fmt, plan-leaks and python-parity, which scripts/pre-commit evaluates pre-merge once the hook is installed; and the E4 widened diff window at check-allow-rationale.sh:368 is excluded, because ci.yml:287-289 documents the origin/main fallback as the push-event behaviour and its effect is over-scoping, not lost enforcement.

- **Station:** build-ci — build/CI/scripts/schemas/docs (lens architecture; ingest ref architecture-02)
- **Baseline:** `077dbe2c287b92c2d0c6a12d5f67c2c0cb83c39c`
- **Anchors:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:6`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:4`, `scripts/ci/check-allow-rationale.sh:422`
- **Enforcement:** blocking — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `quality-scripts`, step "Check rationale on new suppressions (E4 gate)" (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:292`) — gate-census.json row for scripts/ci/check-allow-rationale.sh
- **Evidence:** The trigger block is asymmetric: `push` covers main AND develop (:4-5), `pull_request` covers main only (:6-7). A pull request whose base is develop therefore triggers no ci.yml run; the first evaluation of that change happens on the post-merge push. All 14 jobs are affected, including the 13 blocking gates wired in `quality-scripts` (:248-300) -- genericity (:262), cut-selection determinism (:264), comment refs (:276), doc paths (:274), plan leaks (:270), python parity (:294), doc voice (:296) -- plus clippy (:154), fmt (:246), schemas (:339) and docs-examples (:360). A failure on develop is detected on a branch that already contains the defect, so the gate reports rather than prevents. The E4 allow-rationale gate compounds this: its base is `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` (:368) over `crates/*/src/*.rs` (:422), so on a develop push its diff window is the whole develop-versus-main delta rather than the one change, and its per-change scoping is lost exactly where the PR run is missing. `git show 077dbe2c:.github/workflows/ci.yml | sed -n '3,7p'; git grep -n 'pull_request' 077dbe2c -- .github/workflows; git show 077dbe2c:scripts/ci/check-allow-rationale.sh | sed -n '368p;422p'`
- **Fix-shape:** One sentence, as the probe directs: the trigger list is the owner's call, and the shape that removes the asymmetry is to have the pull_request trigger cover the same branch set the push trigger already covers. Everything else follows from that one edit; no job, gate or script changes.
- **Alignment:** neutral (provisional; Epic 9 adjudicates against the L0-L4 target-layering brief — advances no phase; a trigger-list decision (Part V.0 pull, don't push honoured — no new workflow))
- **Reviewer rating:** A — downgraded to B: one edit site (the pull_request branch filter) bounds the blast radius; no structure spreads and every gate still runs on the post-merge push
- **Calibration:** ci.yml alone carries the gap (pull_request [main] :6-7 against push [main, develop] :4-5); one trigger list is the whole blast radius and the owner may hold post-merge detection on develop to be intended.
- **Needs-human (owner gate):** Owner call on the trigger list: extend ci.yml's pull_request filter to [main, develop], accepting a full ci.yml run on every develop pull request, or ratify post-merge detection on develop as the intended trade and record that rationale in the workflow or a design doc, since no text at the pin states it.
- **Queued to:** owner gate only (no downstream queue)

**CD-101 · Sev B · asymmetry · effort S · confidence high**
Both invariance-shuffle.yml run lines (:34 and :55) omit cobre-sddp's own test-support feature, so the parity target they name fails to compile at the pin (lib.rs:46-47 gates pub mod test_support, which parity.rs:752-1461 uses unconditionally, and Cargo.toml:77 only enables cobre-core's like-named feature): the residue is that the FULL_SHUFFLE_PERMUTATIONS sweep behind the bare ignore at parity.rs:139-163 and its CLP twin at :298-322 has no working invocation in the tree, NOT that declaration-order invariance is unverified in CI, since the i = 0 permutation folded into each parity_hash_<case> test (parity.rs:28-32) runs on both backends via ci.yml:114 and ci.yml:233 under NON_SOLVER_FEATURES (ci.yml:32), which carries both slow-tests and test-support.

- **Station:** build-ci — build/CI/scripts/schemas/docs (lens architecture; ingest ref architecture-03)
- **Baseline:** `077dbe2c287b92c2d0c6a12d5f67c2c0cb83c39c`
- **Anchors:** `.github/workflows/invariance-shuffle.yml:34`, `.github/workflows/invariance-shuffle.yml:55`, `crates/cobre-sddp/Cargo.toml:55`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:114`
- **Enforcement:** blocking — `.github/workflows/invariance-shuffle.yml` job `shuffle-highs`, step "Full shuffle matrix (HiGHS)" — defender verdict (workflow subject, not a scripts/ci gate row)
- **Evidence:** Four facts compose into a dead path. (1) Both workflow invocations pass features but not `test-support`: `--features slow-tests` at :34 and `--no-default-features --features "clp slow-tests"` at :55. (2) `pub mod test_support` in the library is gated `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]` at lib.rs:46-47; an integration test links the library built WITHOUT cfg(test), so the module exists only when the feature is passed. (3) The `parity` target needs it unconditionally: `mod determinism` at parity.rs:752 is ungated (line 751 is blank, 750 closes the preceding module) and calls `cobre_sddp::test_support::fill_consistent_basis` at :894, with three further unconditional uses at :1303, :1437 and :1461. (4) The crate's own `test-support` feature at Cargo.toml:55 is not reachable by accident: the dev-dependency at :77 enables `cobre-core/test-support`, a DIFFERENT crate's feature, which does not turn on cobre-sddp's. So both dispatched commands fail at compile time, before any shuffle test is selected. The automatic suite does not compensate: the five shuffle tests carry a plain `#[ignore = "full shuffle matrix -- dispatched via invariance-shuffle.yml"]` (parity.rs:139, :145, :151, :157, :163 -- not the slow-tests cfg_attr form used elsewhere), and ci.yml:114 runs `cargo test --workspace` with no `--include-ignored`, so they are skipped there too. The workflow is also `workflow_dispatch`-only, with the nightly schedule commented out at :5-7, so nothing ever surfaces the compile failure automatically. Net: the declaration-order-invariance contract at CLAUDE.md:26-31 has a shuffle matrix that no CI path can execute. `git show 077dbe2c:.github/workflows/invariance-shuffle.yml | sed -n '3,7p;32,35p;53,56p'; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-sddp/Cargo.toml | sed -n '46p;55p;77p'; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-sddp/src/lib.rs | sed -n '46,47p'; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-sddp/tests/parity.rs | sed -n '752p;894p'; git show 077dbe2c:.github/workflows/ci.yml | sed -n '114p'`
- **Fix-shape:** Amend the two existing run lines so the feature set they pass actually satisfies the target they name: the parity binary needs the crate's own `test-support` feature alongside the backend and slow-tests features, on both the primary-backend and the secondary-backend invocation. That is the whole compile fix. Two further decisions surround it and are named, not taken here. First, the ignore form: these five tests use a bare ignore rather than the slow-tests cfg_attr pattern the rest of the crate uses, which is why the automatic suite cannot reach them even with the workspace feature set; converting them to the crate's established gating form would let the main suite run them whenever the feature is on, and would make the dispatch-only workflow a convenience rather than the sole path. Second, the trigger: a manually dispatched workflow cannot report a regression nobody dispatched, so the owner should decide between restoring the commented-out schedule and folding the matrix into an automatically triggered job. A cheap guard against the whole class is worth stating: an automatically triggered compile-only step over this test target would have caught the missing feature immediately, since the failure is at compile time and needs no shuffle run.
- **Alignment:** neutral (provisional; Epic 9 adjudicates against the L0-L4 target-layering brief — advances no phase; amends two existing run lines (Part V.0))
- **Reviewer rating:** A — downgraded to B: the workflow is workflow_dispatch-only (its schedule is commented out) and the residue is two feature strings plus the tests' ignore form — bounded, no propagation
- **Calibration:** two run lines in a dispatch-only workflow pass a feature set that cannot compile the parity target they name; the surviving residue is that the FULL_SHUFFLE sweep has no working invocation, not that declaration-order invariance is unprotected (the automatic suite's shuffle tests run).
- **Related:** TD-045 (L4717, cites invariance-shuffle.yml); sddp gate NH9 (R6-nh-9) → E07.
- **Needs-human (owner gate):** Shuffle-matrix reachability is an owner call: restore the commented-out nightly schedule at invariance-shuffle.yml:5-7, or convert the bare-ignore shuffle tests to the crate's slow-tests cfg_attr form so the automatically triggered suite runs them and the dispatch workflow becomes a convenience.
- **Needs-human (owner gate):** Whether the compile-only guard against this class (a target-compiling step over the parity test binary under the shuffle feature set) is wanted at all, given that ci.yml:114 and :233 already compile that target under a feature set that works.

**CD-102 · Sev B · asymmetry · effort S · confidence high**
No guard in the corpus compares the canonical examples/1dtoy/ file SET against either hand-maintained enumeration (build.rs TEMPLATE_FILES at :16, templates.rs DTOY1_FILES), so the single escaping edit is ADDING a presence-discovered optional input file to the canonical deck without changing any already-embedded file's bytes; canonical deletion is caught by the expect at templates.rs:210 and modification (including any addition that config.json references) by the assert_eq! at templates.rs:212, and check-docs-examples.sh:113 is conceded to meet its own declared CLI-output-shape contract rather than being a deficient mirror guard, with the resulting drift being divergence from the documented canonical deck rather than a broken or unrunnable init output.

- **Station:** build-ci — build/CI/scripts/schemas/docs (lens architecture; ingest ref architecture-04)
- **Baseline:** `077dbe2c287b92c2d0c6a12d5f67c2c0cb83c39c`
- **Anchors:** `crates/cobre-cli/build.rs::TEMPLATE_FILES`, `scripts/ci/check-docs-examples.sh:32`, `scripts/ci/check-docs-examples.sh:113`
- **Enforcement:** blocking — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `docs-examples`, step "Verify init/run structural invariants" (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:360`) — gate-census.json row for scripts/ci/check-docs-examples.sh
- **Evidence:** build.rs:8-9 states the invariant in prose -- `examples/1dtoy/` is canonical and `templates/1dtoy/` must be kept in sync BY HAND -- and `const TEMPLATE_FILES` is the embedded enumeration. Content equality IS guarded, and the naive claim that nothing checks it is false: a unit test byte-compares each embedded file against the canonical file on disk and runs in the workspace suite (see positives). The surviving hole is directional. Both guards iterate the embedded set: the unit test walks the embedded files and asserts each matches its canonical counterpart, and the shell gate at :113 counts the files that `cobre init` WROTE and compares that count to `EXPECTED_INPUT_FILES=11` -- which is the embedded cardinality, so the assert is a tautology with respect to TEMPLATE_FILES and says nothing about the canonical tree. Nothing reads the canonical directory: no script or workflow mentions `examples/1dtoy` at all, and the corpus's only recursive diff is check_schemas.sh:31 over `schemas/`. Consequence: add a twelfth file to `examples/1dtoy/` and forget TEMPLATE_FILES, and every guard stays green while `cobre init --template 1dtoy` silently produces a deck the documented canonical case does not match. `git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-cli/build.rs | sed -n '8,9p;16p'; git show 077dbe2c:scripts/ci/check-docs-examples.sh | sed -n '32p;111,116p'; git grep -nE 'diff -r|diff -ru|cmp ' 077dbe2c -- scripts .github/workflows; git grep -n 'examples/1dtoy' 077dbe2c -- scripts .github/workflows`
- **Fix-shape:** Amend the existing blocking gate rather than adding one. The gate already has the canonical directory available at the workspace root and already knows the template name, so the missing assertion is a set comparison rather than a count: compare the file set the canonical directory contains against the file set `cobre init` materializes, and fail when either side has a member the other lacks. That subsumes the current count assert, removes the hand-maintained expected-count literal from the script, and closes the direction the unit test cannot see because the unit test's iteration domain is the embedded list itself. The build script's prose invariant at :8-9 then describes something a gate enforces instead of something a person remembers.
- **Alignment:** neutral (provisional; Epic 9 adjudicates against the L0-L4 target-layering brief — advances no phase; amends the existing blocking gate (Part V.0))
- **Calibration:** the template mirror is guarded for deletion and modification but not for a file added to the canonical deck; one blocking gate plus one const bound the fix (CD-010 precedent: named edit sites).
- **Needs-human (owner gate):** Is examples/1dtoy/ contractually EQUAL to what cobre init materializes, or a superset allowed to carry non-input files as examples/4ree/README.md does? The answer decides whether the missing assertion is set equality or one-way canonical-subset inclusion.
- **Queued to:** owner gate only (no downstream queue)

**CD-103 · Sev B · asymmetry · effort S · confidence high**
Only the `[lints.clippy]` table at `crates/cobre-python/Cargo.toml:50-55`, including `unwrap_used = deny`, is evaluated by no step at the pin, and the gap is a documented-but-uncarried contributor obligation rather than an unrecognised blind spot: both clippy runs (`ci.yml:154`, `ci.yml:221`) are `--workspace` and the crate is excluded at `Cargo.toml:21-23`, while `CONTRIBUTING.md:216` already states that clippy for this crate needs `--manifest-path` because the workspace-wide invocations skip it, yet neither the contributor checklist at `CONTRIBUTING.md:386` nor the release checklist at `:602-604` carries that command and `scripts/pre-commit` runs no clippy. Excluded from the residue: the sibling `[lints.rust]` table at `:46-48`, which IS evaluated and blocking, because `RUSTFLAGS: -Dwarnings` at `ci.yml:11` escalates `missing_docs` in the two python-job steps that compile the crate (`:559` maturin develop, `:567` cargo test). Also excluded: any live violation, since the ten `.unwrap()` uses all sit under the `#[cfg(test)]` allow at `errors.rs:358-359`.

- **Station:** build-ci — build/CI/scripts/schemas/docs (lens architecture; ingest ref architecture-05)
- **Baseline:** `077dbe2c287b92c2d0c6a12d5f67c2c0cb83c39c`
- **Anchors:** `crates/cobre-python/Cargo.toml:46`, `crates/cobre-python/Cargo.toml:50`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:154`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:221`
- **Enforcement:** blocking — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `clippy`, step "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets" — defender verdict (workflow subject, not a scripts/ci gate row)
- **Evidence:** Every clippy invocation in the repository is `--workspace` (ci.yml:154 in the `clippy` job at :116, ci.yml:221 in the `clp` job at :166); `git grep` finds no third one and none with `--manifest-path`. The bindings crate is excluded from the workspace (root Cargo.toml:21-23), so neither invocation compiles it, and clippy therefore never evaluates the table the crate declares at :50-55 -- `all` and `pedantic` at warn, `unwrap_used = "deny"`, `expect_used` and `panic` at warn. Those are clippy tool lints: rustc ignores them, so the one CI compile of this crate, `cargo test --manifest-path crates/cobre-python/Cargo.toml` at :567, does not evaluate them either. CLAUDE.md:20-21 lists both as non-negotiable hard rules (":17 -- These are non-negotiable"). The crate is not in breach at the pin: all ten `.unwrap()` occurrences in its sources sit in a test module covered by an explicit allow, so this is an uncovered surface rather than a live violation -- the clippy job would stay green if that changed. The asymmetry is sharpest against the E4 gate, which is blocking at ci.yml:292 and scopes its diff to `crates/*/src/*.rs` at check-allow-rationale.sh:422: that glob DOES match the bindings crate, so a new `#[allow(clippy::...)]` there must carry a written rationale for a lint no CI job ever runs, and the crate already carries around twenty such suppressions. The seeded `doc = false` at :18 is a separate and much smaller fact: the docs job's `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` at :399 never sees the crate anyway because of the same exclusion, so that line changes nothing about CI coverage and is inert here. `git grep -n 'cargo clippy\|cargo doc' 077dbe2c -- .github scripts; git show 077dbe2c:Cargo.toml | sed -n '21,23p'; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-python/Cargo.toml | sed -n '15,18p;43,50p'; git show 077dbe2c:CLAUDE.md | sed -n '20,21p'; git show 077dbe2c:scripts/ci/check-allow-rationale.sh | sed -n '422p'`
- **Fix-shape:** Amend the job that already exists rather than reopening the exclusion. The workspace exclusion is sanctioned and states its own reason, so the fix is not to make the crate a member; it is to give the crate the same lint pass every member gets, at the one place in CI that already builds it with a Python interpreter present. The python job already compiles this crate against its own manifest for the Rust tests, on a single matrix entry, so a clippy pass over the same manifest with warnings denied belongs beside that step and inherits its interpreter and its backend feature selection. Two secondary points for the owner. The same membership boundary means the crate is outside the documentation-warning bar as well, so whoever adds the clippy pass should decide whether a docs pass over the manifest is worth the minutes, given that the crate's rustdoc is user-facing for Python readers. And once clippy runs, the roughly twenty existing clippy suppressions in the crate become meaningful for the first time, so expect the first run to surface work; that is the finding, not a side effect of the fix.
- **Alignment:** neutral (provisional; Epic 9 adjudicates against the L0-L4 target-layering brief — advances no phase (the defender's advances-0a reading — the bindings as an L4 entry point — does not make a lint step part of the Engine seam; Part IV.4 is not touched))

- **Reviewer rating:** A — downgraded to B: one manifest-scoped clippy step beside the existing bindings' test step closes it; the rustc-side bar already reaches the crate, so no structure spreads
- **Calibration:** only the crate-local `[lints.clippy]` table (incl. unwrap_used = deny) is evaluated by no CI step; RUSTFLAGS -Dwarnings does reach the crate through its tests, and CONTRIBUTING.md:216 already documents the manifest-scoped command — a documented-but-uncarried obligation with a one-step fix.

The eight Build steps sit at :49 :87 :130 :180 :316 :377 :468 :522, one in each of eight of the fourteen jobs (check :35, test :73, clippy :116, clp :166, schemas :302, docs :363, coverage :454, python :504). Two further consumers live outside ci.yml and are VARIANTS, not copies: mpi-slurm.yml:63 (triple :56-84) adds set -euo pipefail to the Set step at :81 and drops the LD_LIBRARY_PATH export that ci.yml:68 makes; release-mpi.yml:75 (triple :67-100) guards all three steps with matrix.mpi_source == 'source' at :68 :76 :96, carries a four-line ch3:nemesis runtime/ABI comment at :82-85, renames the third step Set MPICH environment (Linux) at :95, and also drops LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Ten consumers in total. git ls-tree of .github/ returns the single entry workflows, so no actions/ directory exists to hold a composite action today. `for r in 81,106 124,149 174,199 310,335 371,396 462,487 516,541; do diff <(git show 077dbe2c:.github/workflows/ci.yml | sed -n '43,68p') <(git show 077dbe2c:.github/workflows/ci.yml | sed -n "${r}p") >/dev/null && echo "IDENTICAL to 43-68: $r"; done; git show 077dbe2c:.github/workflows/ci.yml | grep -n 'Build MPICH from source'; git ls-tree --name-only 077dbe2c .github/`
- **Fix-shape:** Extract the Cache/Build/Set triple into one composite action under a new .github/actions/ directory and have all ten sites use it. The action takes the MPICH version, an input for the matrix guard so release-mpi.yml can keep its matrix.mpi_source == 'source' condition without a second copy, and an input for the LD_LIBRARY_PATH export that the two out-of-file variants currently drop, so the one intentional difference between the ci.yml copies and the variants becomes a declared parameter instead of an undocumented divergence. This amends the existing workflows rather than adding a framework, and rule 6's one-consumer objection does not apply: the triple has ten present consumers, so the abstraction follows its consumers rather than anticipating them. The ch3:nemesis rationale comment that only release-mpi.yml carries moves into the action so every consumer inherits it.
- **Pull-don't-push:** one-consumer objection waived: 8 `Build MPICH from source` steps in ci.yml plus 1 in mpi-slurm.yml and 1 in release-mpi.yml consume the block (10 call sites) against an absent .github/actions/ directory — a composite action is a normal candidate, not a conflicts row.

**CD-113 · Sev B · duplication · effort S · confidence high**
At the pin the base image has two unlinked version decisions, not three: the ARG default at tests/slurm/Dockerfile.base:42 fixes what is compiled and slurm-base-image.yml:14 fixes the tag pushed at :41, with no build-args key in the :35-44 build step joining them, so bumping either alone publishes an image whose tag misnames its MPICH; the pushed tag is not a separate owner because :41 interpolates :14. A separate third literal at tests/slurm/Dockerfile:15 decides what the cluster image builds FROM, because neither build block in tests/slurm/docker-compose.yml passes args, which is why the tag pulled at mpi-slurm.yml:106 is not the tag consumed.

- **Station:** build-ci — build/CI/scripts/schemas/docs (lens over-engineering; ingest ref over-engineering-01)
- **Baseline:** `077dbe2c287b92c2d0c6a12d5f67c2c0cb83c39c`
- **Anchors:** `tests/slurm/Dockerfile.base:42`, `tests/slurm/Dockerfile.base:8`, `tests/slurm/Dockerfile:15`
- **Evidence:** One version value is hand-written in at least nine places across four workflows and two Dockerfiles, and three of them are independent OWNERS rather than consumers of a single source. slurm-base-image.yml builds tests/slurm/Dockerfile.base through docker/build-push-action@v7 (:35-44) and passes no build-args, so the version actually compiled is decided solely by the ARG default at Dockerfile.base:42, while the tag pushed at :41 is interpolated from that workflow's own env at :14. Nothing forces the two to agree, so bumping one and not the other publishes an image tagged 4.2.3 that contains a different MPICH. A third owner consumes the result: mpi-slurm.yml:106 pulls slurm-mpich-base:${MPICH_VERSION} resolved from its own env at :33, and tests/slurm/Dockerfile:15 pins the same tag again as a literal in its BASE_IMAGE default. The comment at Dockerfile.base:8 states the rebuild trigger is a change to that file or to MPICH_VERSION in the ci env, but slurm-base-image.yml's path filter (:5-8) watches only tests/slurm/Dockerfile.base and the workflow file itself, so a ci.yml version bump triggers no rebuild and no re-tag. The ch4:ofi device at Dockerfile.base:54 differs deliberately from the ch3:nemesis device the workflow copies configure, so this is a genuinely separate artifact and not a fourth copy of the candidate above. `git grep -nE 'MPICH_VERSION|MPICH 4\.2\.3|slurm-mpich-base:' 077dbe2c -- '.github/workflows' 'tests/slurm'; git show 077dbe2c:.github/workflows/slurm-base-image.yml | grep -nE 'build-args|args:' || echo 'NO build-args passed'`
- **Fix-shape:** Give the version one owner and make every other site derive from it. The base-image workflow passes the version to docker/build-push-action as a build-arg so the ARG default in Dockerfile.base stops being an independent decision, and the pushed tag and the built version then come from the same expression. The pinned literal in tests/slurm/Dockerfile's BASE_IMAGE default and the pull in mpi-slurm.yml both take the tag from that same value rather than repeating it. The prose rebuild-trigger claim at Dockerfile.base:8 is then either made true by adding the workflow path that carries the version to the base-image workflow's path filter, or corrected to describe the filter that exists. The composite action proposed for the MPICH step triple takes the version as an input for the same reason, so both fixes converge on one source rather than introducing a second mechanism.
- **Alignment:** neutral (provisional; Epic 9 adjudicates against the L0-L4 target-layering brief — advances no phase; amends the existing image workflow (Part V.0))
- **Calibration:** two unlinked owners of the MPICH version in the SLURM image path (Dockerfile.base:42 ARG default vs slurm-base-image.yml:14 tag, no build-arg joining them) plus a third literal deciding the cluster image's base — a release-artifact mislabel risk bounded to tests/slurm/ and one workflow.
- **Queued to:** owner gate only (no downstream queue)

**CD-115 · Sev B · duplication · effort S · confidence high**
The crates.io release set exists only as eight literal crate names in the publish step body at publish.yml:80-103, with no publish key in the root manifest or any crates/*/Cargo.toml at the pin and no step comparing that list against the thirteen members at Cargo.toml:4-17, so the exclusion of a workspace member is recorded nowhere and a newly added or promoted member is skipped while the step still exits zero; conceded as over-reach are the inference of publication intent from the reserved manifests description prose and the step-name and success-echo wording, which are cosmetic.

- **Station:** build-ci — build/CI/scripts/schemas/docs (lens over-engineering; ingest ref over-engineering-05)
- **Baseline:** `077dbe2c287b92c2d0c6a12d5f67c2c0cb83c39c`
- **Anchors:** `.github/workflows/publish.yml:36`, `.github/workflows/publish.yml:80`, `.github/workflows/publish.yml:105`, `Cargo.toml:12`, `crates/cobre-mcp/Cargo.toml:3`
- **Enforcement:** blocking — `.github/workflows/publish.yml` job `publish`, step "Publish all crates" — defender verdict (workflow subject, not a scripts/ci gate row)
- **Evidence:** Diffing the member list at Cargo.toml:4-17 against the crate names the publish step actually submits shows exactly five members present in the manifest and absent from the workflow, and they are the five reserved ones. The workflow's ordered list at :80 :84 :85 :86 :90 :94 :98 :103 is written by hand in dependency layers with prose comments, the step that runs it is named Publish all crates at :36, and it ends by echoing All crates published successfully at :105, so both the step name and the success message assert a set five members wider than the list. One omission is documented: an inline comment states that cobre-python goes to PyPI via maturin rather than crates.io, which matches its workspace exclusion at Cargo.toml:21-23. The five reserved members have no such note anywhere in the workflow, and grep finds no publish key in any of their manifests, so nothing in the manifests marks them unpublishable either. Their manifests point the other way: cobre-mcp/Cargo.toml:3 carries the description Reserved crate name. The Cobre MCP server is not yet implemented; depend on cobre-cli for command-line interaction with Cobre, which is prose written for a crates.io reader, and each reserved manifest inherits the workspace version. So the two artifacts disagree about intent and no guard forces the question: if the reserved names are meant to hold their place on the registry, the release never refreshes them; if they are not meant to be published, the manifests do not say so and only a hand-written list keeps them out. Either way, the day a reserved crate becomes real, the publish list stays silent and the release still reports success. `diff <(git show 077dbe2c:Cargo.toml | sed -n '4,17p' | tr -d ' ",' | sort) <(git show 077dbe2c:.github/workflows/publish.yml | grep -oE '^ +publish cobre[a-z-]*' | awk '{print "crates/"$2}' | sort); git grep -n 'publish' 077dbe2c -- 'crates/cobre-mcp/Cargo.toml' 'crates/cobre-tui/Cargo.toml' 'crates/cobre-flow/Cargo.toml' 'crates/cobre-uc/Cargo.toml' 'crates/cobre-emt/Cargo.toml' || echo 'no publish key in any reserved manifest'`
- **Fix-shape:** Make the intent explicit at one site and let the workflow derive from it rather than restate it. Either add publish = false to the five reserved manifests, which puts the decision next to the crate it describes and lets the workflow assert that every member is either in its ordered list or marked unpublishable, or add the five to the list at the layer that has no intra-workspace dependencies, which is where they belong since their dependency tables are empty. In both cases the reconciliation is a few lines inside the existing Publish all crates step comparing the member list against the list plus the opt-outs, so the workflow fails loudly instead of echoing success over a silent omission, and no new gate script or framework is introduced. The step name and the closing message are corrected to name the set that is actually published if any member stays out by design.
- **Alignment:** neutral (provisional; Epic 9 adjudicates against the L0-L4 target-layering brief — advances no phase; amends the existing publish step (Part V.0))
- **Calibration:** the crates.io release set exists only as eight literal names in publish.yml:80-103 with no `publish` key in any manifest and no reconciliation against the thirteen members — a hand-mirror of the member list whose silent-skip failure is bounded to the release workflow.
- **Needs-human (owner gate):** Owner policy call: are the five reserved crate names meant to be re-published at every release so they keep holding their place on crates.io (their manifests inherit the workspace version and set no publish key), or is their absence from the publish list the intended policy that the manifests should state with publish = false? The tree states neither, so the fix direction is an owner decision, not a reading.
- **Queued to:** owner gate only (no downstream queue)

Name the trade-off honestly for the owner, because it is real and it is the owner's call: a populator edge serializes the whole workflow behind one job even on a warm key, where today every consumer restores in parallel and nothing waits. A second, weaker shape avoids that by leaving the graph alone and only removing consumers, which is what the schemas and python entries do; the two shapes compose, and doing the consumer removal first shrinks the population the ordering question applies to.

- **Anchors:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:337`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:339`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:358`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:360`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:545`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:561`, `scripts/ci/check_schemas.sh:23`, `scripts/ci/check-docs-examples.sh:86`
- **Enforcement:** blocking — the workflow jobs the shape sits on
- **Evidence:** The same release binary is produced by three job definitions: schemas via check_schemas.sh:23, docs-examples via check-docs-examples.sh:86, and python via `cargo build --release -p cobre-cli` at ci.yml:561, which selects the same target because cobre-cli declares `[[bin]] name = "cobre"` and no library target. Nothing in the workflow links those three builds: `upload-artifact` and `download-artifact` match nowhere in ci.yml, so no job consumes another's binary, and `shared-key` matches nowhere either, so no rust-cache use is declared as sharing scope with another job. The asymmetry is that the opposite directive is used deliberately three times - `prefix-key` at :209, :495 and :545 - each to SEPARATE a cache, with the clp separation carrying its rationale in a comment. The workflow therefore expresses cache separation explicitly and cache sharing not at all, and the python job multiplies its copy of the build across the matrix at :511.
- **Shape (pointer for the perf epic, no fix here):** Pointer for the perf epic: give the release cobre binary one producer in the workflow and let the consumers receive it, instead of three independent producers. Two shapes, with a genuine trade-off the owner should pick between. First, build once and pass the binary between jobs, which needs the producer job plus a `needs:` edge from each consumer and makes the two script gates accept a prebuilt binary rather than building one - both scripts already separate building from checking behind their `--build` flag, so that seam exists. Second, keep three builders and declare the two that run the identical command as sharing one rust-cache scope, which is a one-line amend per job and does not touch the scripts or the job graph, but leaves the compile itself duplicated on a cold cache. Both are pull-not-push: the first reuses the `--build` seam the scripts already have, the second uses the same rust-cache input the workflow already parameterises three times in the separating direction. State the counter-consideration: separate builds are independent, so one job's broken build cannot mask another's, and the first shape gives that up.
- **Measurement:** UNMEASURED — informational by epic scope (CI wall-time / gate-runtime shape); never promoted to a PD id, never enters the epic-10 sweep; no perf-queue.json is emitted by this station
- **Alignment:** neutral (provisional; informational rows carry no id and are not adjudicated as findings)
- **Needs-human (owner gate):** Owner call: whether the release cobre binary gets one producer plus a publish/consume edge — which would be the first needs: edge in `ci.yml` (none at the pin, so every job is independent today) and would let one broken build block the consumers instead of each gate surfacing its own — or stays duplicated per job; the candidate's second shape, a shared rust-cache scope, is not an alternative to that decision, since a cache scope does not hand a built binary to another job.

**Informational · UNMEASURED · performance-05**
At exactly two ci.yml sites, the cargo-audit install in the security job at :413 and the cargo-llvm-cov install in the coverage job at :496, both of which carry the locked flag alone with no version pin and no feature selection, the from-source acquisition is an asymmetry no adjacent comment or repository document explains against the prebuilt-binary install action the same workflow already wires at :215-217; the license-notices site at :443 is excluded from the claim because its exact version pin plus feature selection makes prebuilt availability unverifiable at the baseline.

- **Station:** build-ci — build/CI/scripts/schemas/docs (lens performance, informational; ingest ref performance-05)
- **Baseline:** `077dbe2c287b92c2d0c6a12d5f67c2c0cb83c39c`
- **Anchors:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:215`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:217`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:413`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:443`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:496`, `.github/workflows/invariance-shuffle.yml:29`, `.github/workflows/invariance-shuffle.yml:50`
- **Enforcement:** blocking — the workflow jobs the shape sits on
- **Evidence:** The prebuilt-binary install action is already a wired dependency of this repository's CI: it appears at ci.yml:215 to install nextest, with `tool: nextest` at :217, and twice more in invariance-shuffle.yml at :29 and :50. Three other ci.yml jobs instead build their tool from source in the job: security at :413, license-notices at :443 and coverage at :496. All three of the from-source installs are `--locked`, and the license one additionally pins `--version 0.9.0`, so the reproducibility intent is explicit and must survive any amend. The asymmetry is in the acquisition method only, not in the pinning discipline.
- **Shape (pointer for the perf epic, no fix here):** Pointer for the perf epic and a pull-not-push amend: acquire the three tools the same way the workflow already acquires nextest, through the install action that is already a dependency here, keeping each tool's existing version pin as the action's version input so the current reproducibility guarantee is unchanged. Nothing new is introduced - no new action, no new job, no composite - so this is an amend of an existing pattern to three call sites. Two things the owner should weigh, because they are the reason the current shape may be deliberate. The pinned license tool has an exact version and a feature selection (`--features cli`); if the prebuilt distribution for that version or that feature set does not exist, that call site stays as it is and the amend covers only the other two. And a from-source install exercises the tool's own build, which a prebuilt download does not; if that is valued for the audit tooling, say so in a comment at the call site rather than leaving the asymmetry unexplained, which is the pattern the clp cache separation at :205-206 already sets.
- **Measurement:** UNMEASURED — informational by epic scope (CI wall-time / gate-runtime shape); never promoted to a PD id, never enters the epic-10 sweep; no perf-queue.json is emitted by this station
- **Alignment:** neutral (provisional; informational rows carry no id and are not adjudicated as findings)
- **Needs-human (owner gate):** Whether a prebuilt distribution of cargo-about exists for the exact version pinned at ci.yml:443 together with its cli feature selection is an external fact unverifiable at the baseline, and it decides whether that third site can join the amend at all.
- **Needs-human (owner gate):** Whether the rust-cache action wired at ci.yml:412 and :495 already restores compiled cargo binaries between runs is a property of an action implemented outside this repository, and it decides how much repeated work the two confirmed sites actually carry.

**Informational · UNMEASURED · performance-06**
One workflow-level acquisition choice, not nine defective jobs: the single `submodules: recursive` input repeated at ci.yml:42, 80, 123, 173, 309, 356, 370, 461 and 515 acquires the whole four-entry .gitmodules registry, while crates/cobre-solver/build.rs opens a vendored tree only inside its own feature branch (HiGHS at :30, Clp plus CoinUtils at :182), so the never-compiled tree on a given job is exactly the complement of that job's selected backend: the COIN pair on the eight default-feature jobs and the HiGHS tree on clp (:219). The residue is fetch-time only, with no compile, cache-key or gate consequence (vendored trees are outside the workspace members at Cargo.toml:3-15, the rust-cache prefixes key off manifests, and the crates-walking gates run in the submodule-free quality-scripts job), and no per-job feature configuration can ever make the recursive set exact because the two backends are mutually exclusive by design (cobre-solver/Cargo.toml:16-19, build.rs:28). The surviving claim asserts nothing about the relative size of the four trees and nothing about the build scripts' link demands.

- **Station:** build-ci — build/CI/scripts/schemas/docs (lens performance, informational; ingest ref performance-06)
- **Baseline:** `077dbe2c287b92c2d0c6a12d5f67c2c0cb83c39c`
- **Anchors:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:42`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:173`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:219`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:309`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:356`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:515`, `crates/cobre-solver/build.rs::main`
- **Enforcement:** blocking — the workflow jobs the shape sits on
- **Evidence:** Nine of the fourteen job definitions pass `submodules: recursive` to actions/checkout@v6 (ci.yml:42, :80, :123, :173, :309, :356, :370, :461, :515), which fetches all four vendored trees registered in the submodule config, namely the solver's HiGHS, Clp and CoinUtils trees and the sddp crate's qhull tree. The solver build script compiles each vendored superbuild only under its own feature: HiGHS behind CARGO_FEATURE_HIGHS at build.rs:30 and the Clp/CoinUtils pair behind CARGO_FEATURE_CLP at :182. Exactly one of those two branches is ever live per job: the clp job builds with `--no-default-features --features "clp ..."` (ci.yml:219, :221, :223), so it fetches the HiGHS tree and never compiles it, and every other submodule-fetching job builds with the default highs feature, so each fetches the Clp and CoinUtils trees and never compiles them. The qhull tree is the counter-case and is cited so the entry does not overreach: cobre-sddp/build.rs:11 states it reads no CARGO_FEATURE_* variables, so it is compiled unconditionally and its fetch is needed everywhere.
- **Shape (pointer for the perf epic, no fix here):** Pointer for the perf epic, and the honest part of the pointer is that the obvious amend is not available: actions/checkout has no per-submodule selection input, so `submodules: recursive` is all-or-nothing and there is no one-line version of this fix. The shape that does exist is to stop asking checkout for submodules on the jobs where the set is wrong and initialise the needed trees explicitly in a following step, which trades one line for a few on each affected job and moves the submodule list into the workflow where it can drift from the submodule config. That trade-off is the owner's call and the entry does not presume it: uniform recursive checkout is a defensible choice precisely because it cannot drift. Two narrower shapes are worth putting in front of the owner alongside it: apply the change only to the clp job, which is the single asymmetric case and the one whose unused tree is the largest of the four; or leave the checkout alone and record in a comment that the vendored set is fetched whole deliberately, which is what the docs-examples rationale comment does for its own minimal setup. This entry claims nothing about the build scripts themselves - the two feature gates are cited as context, and the link-demand facts at that level are another station's.
- **Measurement:** UNMEASURED — informational by epic scope (CI wall-time / gate-runtime shape); never promoted to a PD id, never enters the epic-10 sweep; no perf-queue.json is emitted by this station
- **Alignment:** neutral (provisional; informational rows carry no id and are not adjudicated as findings)
- **Needs-human (owner gate):** Whether a job-tailored submodule set is acceptable at all: actions/checkout exposes no per-submodule input, so the only tailored shape drops the input and hand-lists submodule paths in a following step on each affected job, creating a second copy of the four-entry .gitmodules registry inside the workflow with no guard pinning the two together; the owner decides whether that duplication is worth the avoided fetch, and the pointer is inert until they do.

### New finding minted at reconciliation (2026-09-11) — found while mapping the Tier-2 seams

**CD-072 · Sev A · asymmetry · effort S · confidence high**
Every out-of-sample class sampler was seeded from the study's root forward seed with no class discriminator anywhere in the derivation, so a deck that set two or more of `inflow`, `load`, `ncs` to `out_of_sample` drew bit-identical noise for the k-th entity of each class under every noise method (SAA, LHS, Sobol, Halton) — an undeclared perfect cross-class correlation; the shipped decks and every test set only the inflow class, so nothing pinned it.

- **Station:** cobre-stochastic (sub-station sampling) — minted at reconciliation, not at the station gate
- **Baseline:** `0d4c8c22` (develop after the Tier-1 merge)
- **Anchors:** `crates/cobre-stochastic/src/sampling/mod.rs::build_forward_sampler`, `crates/cobre-stochastic/src/sampling/mod.rs::build_class_sampler`, `crates/cobre-stochastic/src/sampling/out_of_sample.rs::fill_uncorrelated`, `crates/cobre-stochastic/src/sampling/out_of_sample.rs::fill_saa`, `crates/cobre-stochastic/src/noise/seed.rs::derive_forward_seed_grouped`
- **Evidence:** the three `build_class_sampler` calls pass the same `forward_seed`; `ClassSampler::fill`'s `OutOfSample` arm builds `FreshNoiseSpec` from `(forward_seed, iteration, scenario, noise_group_id, dim)` only; `fill_saa` seeds `derive_forward_seed_grouped(forward_seed, iteration, scenario, noise_group_id)` and each QMC/LHS point spec maps the same tuple. Reproduced with a throwaway test calling `ClassSampler::OutOfSample { forward_seed: 99, dim: 4 }` and `{ dim: 2 }` with one `ClassSampleRequest`: `output[..2]` identical for all four methods. Supported configuration: `config/mod.rs` tests assert `simulation.load_scheme == OutOfSample`; `stochastic_summary.rs` builds a context with `load: OutOfSample`.
- **Fix-shape:** derive a per-class forward seed at `build_forward_sampler`; keep the inflow class on the root seed so every existing inflow-only deck reproduces bit-for-bit, derive load and NCS with a class tag under a new domain prefix.
- **Alignment:** neutral
- **Status:** fixed (2026-09-11) — `derive_class_forward_seed(root, "load" | "ncs")` in `noise/seed.rs` (`0x02` prefix); inflow unchanged; `sampling::tests::test_out_of_sample_classes_draw_distinct_streams` pins it (fails on the old seeding). `fix/out-of-sample-class-seed` ff2221d1 (merged to develop 2026-09-12). Results change only for decks with two or more out-of-sample classes.

### New findings minted at reconciliation (2026-09-12) — found while executing the Tier-2 wave

**CD-073 · Sev C · bad-naming · effort S · confidence high**
`NoisePointSpec.stage_id` is fed `noise_group_id` at every production call site (`fill_uncorrelated`, `ClassNoiseTables::refill` → `build_table`), and the `stage_id` position on the three precompute constructors receives the group id too; the name predates the wave and was preserved deliberately so the precomputed-vs-direct equivalence tests stayed trustworthy.

- **Station:** cobre-stochastic (sub-station tree-noise) — minted at reconciliation
- **Baseline:** `fe439fc0`
- **Anchors:** `crates/cobre-stochastic/src/tree/point_spec.rs::NoisePointSpec`, `crates/cobre-stochastic/src/sampling/out_of_sample.rs::fill_uncorrelated`, `crates/cobre-stochastic/src/sampling/tables.rs::build_table`
- **Evidence:** every producer writes `stage_id: spec.noise_group_id` or passes `group` into the `stage_id` parameter; the opening-tree callers pass a real stage id. One name, two meanings.
- **Fix-shape:** rename the field (and the constructor parameter) to the seed-tuple role it plays (`noise_group_id`, or a neutral `group_id`), or split the tree-side and forward-side spec constructors so each names its own key. Bit-neutral; a rename touches every equivalence test and the goldens' helper, so it is its own narrow ticket, not folded into another.
- **Alignment:** neutral
- **Status:** fixed (2026-09-14) — `NoisePointSpec.stream_id` (doc: forward-pass producers pass the `noise_group_id`, opening-tree producers the stage id) and `stream_id` on the three `*Precomputed::new` constructors; `generate_*`'s `stage_id`, `derive_stage_seed`, `derive_opening_seed` and `FreshNoiseSpec.stage_id` untouched by the rename; `build_table`'s doc deleted (the naming tension it explained is gone). ticket-009.

**PD-031 · Sev C · asymmetry · effort S · confidence high**
`fill_uncorrelated`'s `Selective` and `HistoricalResiduals` arms emit `tracing::warn!` on every draw before falling back to the sample-average method; under those (unsupported-in-forward) methods the warning fires once per (iteration, scenario, stage) on the hot path.

- **Station:** cobre-stochastic (sub-station sampling) — minted at reconciliation
- **Baseline:** `fe439fc0`
- **Anchors:** `crates/cobre-stochastic/src/sampling/out_of_sample.rs::fill_uncorrelated`
- **Evidence:** the two arms log with the stage id and fall through to `fill_saa`; nothing rate-limits or hoists the warning to sampler construction.
- **Fix-shape:** reject or warn once at `build_forward_sampler` (where the per-stage methods are known) and make the two arms silent fallbacks, or reject the combination at config validation so the arms become unreachable.
- **Alignment:** neutral
- **Status:** fixed (2026-09-14) — `warn_unsupported_forward_noise_methods(class, scheme, stages, noise_methods)` runs once per class in `build_forward_sampler` (only for `OutOfSample`, naming the class via `EntityClass::as_str`, the method(s) and the affected `Stage.id`s); the two draw arms are one silent `Selective | HistoricalResiduals => fill_saa` arm; four `WarnRecorder` tests, one of which draws after construction and asserts no further WARN. `FreshNoiseSpec.stage_id` lost its only production readers and was deleted (owner rejected keeping it alive through error-string reads); the test-only `sample_fresh` takes the stage id explicitly. Allocation guard unchanged. ticket-010.

**TD-034 · Sev C · asymmetry · effort S · confidence high**
`crates/cobre-sddp/tests/common/permute.rs` carries its own `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, so every integration binary that declares `mod common;` compiles and runs those tests inside its own harness; a binary that owns process-global state (the counting-allocator guard) cannot use the aggregator at all and includes `common/builders.rs` by `#[path]` with an include-level `dead_code` allow instead.

- **Station:** cobre-sddp (test corpus) — minted at reconciliation
- **Baseline:** `fe439fc0`
- **Anchors:** `crates/cobre-sddp/tests/common/permute.rs`, `crates/cobre-sddp/tests/common/mod.rs`, `crates/cobre-sddp/tests/forward_sampler_no_alloc.rs`
- **Evidence:** `cargo test -p cobre-sddp --features test-support --test forward_sampler_no_alloc -- --list` showed four tests before the `#[path]` include; nextest's process-per-test isolation hid the coupling on every per-ticket gate, and only the threaded `cargo test` harness (which `ci.yml` runs) exposed it.
- **Fix-shape:** move `permute.rs`'s tests to a binary of their own (or to a `#[cfg(test)]` module gated behind a cargo feature the aggregator does not enable), so `mod common;` never adds tests to a consumer; then the guard can use the aggregator and drop its include-level allow. Fold into the test-support surface work (Tier 4) that already owns `common/`.
- **Alignment:** neutral
- **Status:** fixed (2026-09-15) — `permute.rs`'s tests moved to their own binary, `crates/cobre-sddp/tests/permute_helpers.rs`, so `mod common;` adds no tests to a consumer; the allocation guard `forward_sampler_no_alloc.rs` declares `mod common;` like every other binary and its `--list` shows the one guard test. Closed by `plans/quality-tier45-closeout` ticket-013 (epic-03), commit range `3e90024f..54ab986a` on `develop`; recorded at the Tier-4/5 reconciliation after the register merge exposed the id.

## ★ USER-REPORTED BUG (2026-09-17) — anticipated-commitment delivery reconciliation aborts on sub-kW drift

Minted from a user report ahead of the `sddp` station (unrun; the station inherits this entry and does not
re-mint it). The "no new ID minted" accounting of the post-plan reconciliation above predates this section.

**Report (user log, MPI run, rank 8, iteration 37 of 50, 5.5 h in):**

```
Training   37/50 iter  LB: 3.03102e12  UB: 1.87012e11  gap: -93.8%  fwd: 32035ms / bwd: 493339ms  [05:34:34 < 01:57:33]
rank 8:
error: training error: anticipated commitment -0.00015040481625625826 MW for thermal 70 at stage 47 block 0 lies 0.00015040481625625826 MW outside its delivery generation bound 0 — beyond the solver-drift margin, so this is a genuine over-commitment, not numerical drift
-> this may indicate a software or environment problem
-> report this at https://github.com/cobre-rs/cobre/issues
Abort(4) on node 8 (rank 8 in comm 0): application called MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 4) - process 8
```

**CD-074 · Sev A · bad-abstraction (correctness bug, user-visible abort) · effort M (hotfix S + redesign M) · confidence high**
The delivery-stage reconciliation of a carried anticipated commitment tells solver drift from a modelling
error with two hard-coded constants (`1e-7` relative to the commitment, `1e-5` MW absolute). A carried value
of `−1.5e-4` MW against a `0` MW floor is fifteen times the absolute floor, so a physically impossible
negative commitment — which under the ring's own construction can only be solver-side noise — is classified
as a "genuine over-commitment", the rank returns `SddpError::AnticipatedCommitmentOutOfBounds`, and the whole
MPI job dies through `MPI_Abort` with a user-facing message asserting the opposite of what happened. The
discrimination line has now been recalibrated by production failure three times; the mechanism, not the
constant, is the defect. **Redesign flagged.**

- **Station:** cobre-sddp (LP builder `commitment_reconcile` + `training/stage_solve_prep.rs`) — minted from a user report, not at the station gate
- **Baseline:** `develop` @ `077dbe2c` (mechanism unchanged since `7628d3d0`)
- **Anchors:** `crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/builder/commitment_reconcile.rs::drift_margin`, `crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/builder/commitment_reconcile.rs::reconcile_commitment`, `crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/builder/commitment_reconcile.rs::fill_bound_relaxations`, `crates/cobre-sddp/src/training/stage_solve_prep.rs::StageSolvePrep::reconcile_commitments`, `crates/cobre-sddp/src/error.rs::SddpError::AnticipatedCommitmentOutOfBounds`, `crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/builder/columns.rs::fill_anticipated_slot_columns`, `crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/builder/columns.rs::fill_anticipated_state_columns`, `.claude/rules/sddp.md` § "Delivered commitments reconcile against solver drift; exactness is unreachable"
- **Evidence:**
  - Arithmetic of the report: `under = 0 − (−1.5040e-4) = 1.5040e-4` MW; `drift_margin(−1.5040e-4) = |c|·1e-7 + 1e-5 = 1.0000e-5` MW; `under / margin = 15.04` → `Reconciliation::Violation` → `SddpError::AnticipatedCommitmentOutOfBounds` → exit 4 → `MPI_Abort`. The refused quantity is 150 W of thermal output.
  - The value is negative. Delivery-anchoring bounds the decision column to the delivery stage's `[min_gen, max_gen]`, and the ring carries it through equalities on free `(−inf, +inf)` slot columns (`fill_anticipated_slot_columns`, `fill_anticipated_state_columns`) that are always basic and therefore always factorization-computed — the rule's own explanation of where the drift is born. In this report the floor is `0`, so the negative sign alone proves noise — but that is the instance, not the class. The same factorization error lands on **any** side of **any** delivery-stage bound: a must-run plant (`min_generation_mw > 0`, `fill_thermal_columns`) drifts below a positive floor, a plant at its cap drifts above `max_generation_mw`, and both bounds are **per delivery stage and per block** (`thermal_bounds_at_block`; a commissioning-dormant stage forces `[0, 0]`). The classifier has no notion of the box it is protecting: it measures distance from one crossed bound against a margin sized from the commitment, so it misjudges a positive floor and a cap exactly as it misjudged zero.
  - Third production-driven recalibration of the same guard: the original relax-for-any-overshoot widen (deleted, then found load-bearing); `54882130` reinstated it with margin = the raw `1e-9` primal tolerance and it refused `3.8e-6` MW over a `1593` MW cap in production; `7628d3d0` widened to `1e-7` rel + `1e-5` abs, promising "kilowatt-scale modelling errors are refused exactly as before"; now `1.5e-4` MW is refused at a zero floor. Each incident moved a constant; none changed the classifier's model of where the error comes from.
  - The relative term is anchored to the wrong magnitude. Factorization error on a basic variable scales with the LP's row/RHS magnitudes and the basis conditioning, not with the carried value itself, so near zero only the `1e-5` MW floor acts — 10 W — while the observed noise is 150 W. A commitment of exactly zero (an idle anticipated plant, the common case at most stages) gets the tightest margin of all, which is why this surfaced at a `0` bound and not at a cap.
  - The `Relaxed` arm lowers the generation column's scaled lower bound to `(commitment − margin)/scale < 0`, admitting negative thermal generation into the LP rather than projecting the pinned state back onto the physical box.
  - Severity mismatch: a numerical-noise class terminates the whole MPI job (one rank aborts, every rank dies), losing 37 iterations; the message text ("genuine over-commitment, not numerical drift", "report this at …/issues") is confidently wrong and the users did exactly as told. Re-derive: `sed -n 23,40p crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/builder/commitment_reconcile.rs`; `sed -n 140,180p crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/builder/columns.rs`; `git show -s 7628d3d0 54882130`.
- **Fix-shape:** two layers; the second is the point of this entry — **redesign the mechanism, do not move the constants a fourth time.**
  1. *Hotfix (S, unblocks the reporter, byte-neutral for every in-bounds solve so D34's golden and both backends' parity hold):* **project the pinned commitment onto the actual enforced delivery box** instead of relaxing the LP bound. The box is the delivery stage's per-block `[col_lower·scale, col_upper·scale]` for that thermal — the same enforced (scaled, round-tripped) values `reconcile_commitment` already reads — intersected over the stage's blocks, since one commitment pins every block column; a positive must-run floor and a cap are handled by the same clamp as the zero floor, and a dormant `[0, 0]` stage clamps to zero. Drift past the box on either side is absorbed by the projection up to a margin sized from the box/LP magnitude (never from the commitment); the `Relaxed` arm stops lowering a generation bound below its floor or raising it above its cap.
  2. *Redesign (M, owner-gated):* retire the runtime "genuine over-commitment" verdict. As far as delivery-anchoring holds, a genuine over-commitment can only enter through declared inputs (`past_anticipated_commitments` above the delivery cap), so that check belongs to input validation (cobre-io / setup) and fails loud there, at load time. At solve time the pinned commitment is **projected onto the delivery box** — the intersection over blocks of the delivery stage's enforced per-block `[min, max]` for that thermal, both sides, never a hard-coded zero — a pure deterministic function of the value and the template, so reproducibility and order-invariance hold — and the projection distance is **tallied** (max absolute and relative drift per run, surfaced in the run summary, one `tracing::warn!` past a diagnostic threshold sized from the LP scale rather than the commitment). Nothing on this path aborts. Delete `AnticipatedCommitmentOutOfBounds` or re-scope it to the input validator. Rewrite — never delete — the `.claude/rules/sddp.md` contract: the invariant to keep is "a hair of drift never produces a false `Infeasible`" plus its two forbidden alternatives (unscaling-makes-it-redundant; opt-in hook); the clause this entry retires is "the margin is the discrimination line between solver noise and a modelling error". Tests: keep `anticipated_commitment_drifted_over_cap_is_absorbed`; move `anticipated_commitment_over_cap_seed_is_refused` to an input-validation reject; add regressions seeded a hair below a `0` floor (the report), a hair below a positive must-run floor, a hair above a cap, and against a dormant `[0, 0]` delivery stage, plus one with block-varying bounds so the intersection is pinned. An empty intersection over blocks is an input defect (the fishing equality can never hold) and belongs to the same load-time validator.
- **Alignment:** neutral
- **Status:** open — reported 2026-09-17 by users on an MPI production run; not yet reproduced locally (needs the reporter's deck or a synthetic case: an anticipated thermal idle at its delivery stage, long ring, production-scale LP). Owner to choose hotfix-then-redesign vs redesign-only; either way the redesign gets its own ticket.
- **Side observation (not part of this finding):** the same log shows `LB 3.03e12 > UB 1.87e11` (gap `−93.8%`) at iteration 37. Under a risk-neutral objective the lower bound cannot sit 16× above the forward-pass estimate beyond sampling noise; under CVaR the printed forward statistic is not an upper bound, so this may be benign. Ask the reporter for the risk configuration before treating it as a second defect.
